correctness.rationale: Integrated first moments give Lh=d with L positive definite under connectivity; edge insertion changes both L and degrees. Sherman–Morrison algebra reconstructs the displayed formula without singular cases. An exact exhaustive census of all 171 eligible rooted nonroot link additions in all connected graph orders <=4 verifies strict positive signs; for the sharp order-five witness, an independent 16-state CTMC reward computation reproduces 23 and 21. The infinite family adds independent root-adjacent leaves and is proven exactly.

originality.rationale: The same mathematical model literature and mathematical result comparisons do not imply the fixed single-zealot cumulative dissent edge-addition response together with its sharp 5-agent cutoff; the source papers on transient opinion control, two-zealot equilibrium and Kemeny random-target averages establish adjacent but different claims. The general rooted-walk identity and matrix inverse update are explicitly acknowledged as prior mathematical methods. Residual risk remains of earlier equivalent graph hitting-time intervention work; independent bibliographic review has not occurred.
residual_risks: An earlier exact graph-theoretic result may address fixed-root summed hitting time changes under link insertion; no comprehensive literature-exhaustiveness proof is possible.
The 2003 article has a biased, not immutable, zealot and is background rather than a statement of this model; 2007 and later sources treat immutable zealots more directly.
Time normalization is per nonroot agent rate one; comparing synchronous or single-global-clock definitions without rescaling can mislead.

value.rationale: The expected total number of dissenting agents integrated over physical time is a natural finite measure of campaign resistance with one committed opinion leader. An added ordinary social edge can worsen this cost on every small network yet improve it from the sharp fifth agent onward; the two-unit gain persists at any size by root-leaf extension. The exact rank-one response law gives a graph-specific analytical intervention criterion. The sharp cutoff and intervention interpretation are meaningful beyond textbook matrix manipulations.
